agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Salesforce Agrees to Buy Braze for $5.66B
stories.plain: A $5.66 billion acquisition would merge Braze's customer engagement platform into Salesforce's marketing cloud stack. This reshapes how enterprise marketers buy CEP and CDP capability — fewer independent best-of-breed options, more pressure on rivals like Adobe and HubSpot, and big implications for how AI-driven messaging gets consolidated under one vendor.

stories.head: Demandbase Launches AEO Agent to Help Brands Get Recommended by AI Systems
stories.plain: Demandbase coined the term B2A (business-to-agent) marketing and launched an AI agent that helps brands influence how AI buying agents discover and shortlist vendors. This is a direct product move into Generative Engine Optimization, signaling that B2B go-to-market strategy must now account for AI agents as the primary decision-maker, not humans.

stories.head: isolved Puts AI Agents on the Org Chart with Managers, Performance Records and Escalation Paths
stories.plain: isolved's Agent View formally assigns AI agents a human manager, a performance history and an escalation path — treating them like employees. This is a significant governance model for agentic AI: it creates accountability structures that regulators and enterprise buyers increasingly demand before deploying autonomous systems at scale.

stories.head: ChatGPT Has Many Advertisers but Is Generating Little Ad Revenue
stories.plain: Despite expanded access, lower costs, and new targeting tools, OpenAI's advertising business is not converting volume into meaningful revenue. This matters because it questions whether generative AI platforms can replace traditional ad channels for performance marketers and whether GEO investment will pay off in the near term.

stories.head: How Brands Get Shortlisted When a Consumer's AI Agent Does the Shopping
stories.plain: Robin Ross from Activate Insight explains the practical steps brands must take so that AI shopping agents include them in shortlists rather than filtering them out. As agentic commerce accelerates, the rules for discovery, loyalty and personalization change fundamentally — making this a must-understand topic for any marketer building 2027 strategy.

stories.head: Salesforce agrees to buy Braze for $5.66B; Demandbase launches AEO Agent
stories.plain: Salesforce's $5.66 billion acquisition of Braze is the biggest MarTech deal in years, folding a leading customer engagement platform into Salesforce's stack. Separately, Demandbase debuted an Agent Engine Optimization agent — a direct signal that B2A marketing (reaching AI buying agents, not just humans) is becoming a real budget line.

stories.head: Demandbase launches AI agents for B2A marketing, including AEO Agent
stories.plain: Demandbase released three AI agents built for business-to-agent (B2A) marketing — the idea that AI purchasing agents, not humans, will soon shortlist vendors. The AEO Agent specifically helps brands stay visible inside AI-generated answers and recommendations, making this one of the first products to operationalize Generative Engine Optimization at a B2B scale.

stories.head: Robin Ross on how brands make the shortlist when AI agents do the shopping
stories.plain: A live MAICON session unpacks the strategic reality that AI agents are replacing humans as the first filter in purchase decisions. Ross explains what signals and data structures brands must get right to be surfaced by a consumer's AI agent — a governance and discoverability challenge most marketing teams haven't planned for yet.

stories.head: 72% of marketing teams haven't grown despite faster AI-era delivery demands
stories.plain: Demandbase research shows 72% of B2B marketing teams are the same size or smaller than two years ago, while 70% face faster turnaround expectations. This data quantifies the core pressure driving AI tool adoption — not innovation appetite but headcount math — making it essential context for anyone buying or building marketing AI.

stories.head: ChatGPT has plenty of advertisers but ad revenue lags expectations
stories.plain: OpenAI expanded access and added targeting tools, yet advertiser volume hasn't converted to meaningful ad revenue. This matters for budget planning: it signals that AI-native ad inventory is still immature, and brands testing ChatGPT placements should temper ROI expectations while the pricing and measurement infrastructure catches up.

themes.head: AI Agents Join the Org Chart
body: The most consequential structural shift this month is that AI agents are being given named roles inside organizations — not just tools that assist people, but entities that sit alongside them on org charts and own workflows. isolved is listing agents as workforce members; Demandbase is framing its launch as the start of a "B2A" (Business-to-Agent) era, implying that the buyer in many B2B journeys is now an AI, not a human.

This forces an immediate strategic question: if an AI agent is doing the shortlisting and the purchasing research, your brand must be legible to machines, not just humans. Robin Ross's MAICON talk made this explicit — getting on the shortlist now means optimizing for agent comprehension, not just human appeal. The decision about how to structure marketing teams and who (or what) owns which tasks can no longer be deferred.

themes.head: AI Search Rewrites Customer Research Behavior
body: Prompts are the new search queries — and the implications for how brands are discovered are profound. When customers type natural-language questions into AI search interfaces, they bypass traditional keyword-indexed results and get synthesized answers. This changes which brands surface, how they are described, and whether voice-of-the-customer programs even capture the signals that matter.

The martech.org analysis argues that VoC programs need urgent redesign to listen at the prompt layer, not just at the review or survey layer. Combined with the observation that AI search is now conducting customer research on behalf of buyers, marketers face a world where brand narrative must be consistently embedded in the training & retrieval layer of AI systems — a fundamentally different content and data strategy than SEO.

themes.head: The Metrics & Measurement Crisis
body: Two separate but connected pieces this month landed on the same diagnosis: the metrics marketers are optimizing are actively degrading decision quality. Chasing incremental performance improvements is cannibalizing creative ambition, and the KPIs teams report on are teaching people to prioritize the measurable over the meaningful. Nearly three-quarters of marketing teams report no headcount growth even as AI pressure mounts — suggesting efficiency gains are being absorbed rather than reinvested in strategic capability.

The core decision shift: stop letting measurement infrastructure dictate strategy. Organizations need to audit whether their metrics reward short-term conversion at the expense of brand equity and team growth. This is especially urgent heading into Cyber Five, where Acoustic's research shows a persistent marketer-shopper disconnect — marketers believe their peak-season messaging is landing far better than shoppers report.

themes.head: AI-Native Creative Tooling Goes Production-Ready
body: This month saw a cluster of AI creative tools crossing from experimental to production-grade: Kling 4.0 launched globally with professional-quality video & multimodal control; Picsart opened a Marketing Studio that creates, tests, and runs Google Ads end-to-end; and AdFury introduced agentic below-the-fold rich media on Walmart. The common signal is that AI creative is no longer a prototype — it is the production pipeline.

For marketing leaders this collapses the traditional briefing-to-publish cycle and makes the question of who reviews, approves, and governs AI-generated creative immediately operational. Brand safety, tone consistency, and legal clearance processes built for human-authored content are not equipped for the volume and speed these tools enable. Governance frameworks need to catch up before the creative pipeline fully automates.

themes.head: Marketing Leadership Must Design Work, Not Just Direct It
body: The most durable leadership insight surfacing this month is that the next generation of marketing executives will be architects of human-AI workflows, not just managers of human teams. MarTech's analysis argues that designing how work gets done — which tasks go to agents, which require human judgment, and how hand-offs are structured — is now a core leadership competency, not an IT or ops concern.

This connects directly to the programmatic finding from StackAdapt: top-performing advertisers are twice as likely to expand their channel mix, suggesting that leaders who actively redesign their operational model outperform those who optimize within existing structures. The implication is that org design, workflow architecture, and AI integration are now the same conversation as marketing strategy.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — creative, search, measurement, org design, and commerce — AI is shifting from assistant to autonomous actor, and the marketers who will win are those who redesign their strategies, metrics, and leadership practices around that reality rather than bolting AI onto what already exists.
